text:
nina: Heads-up — since the role-matrix-v2 rollout last night, a couple of Editor reports that they cannot start live sessions in the Console. Seen any alerts?

sam: Yep, I noticed a spike of 403s on /api/v1/projects/:id/sessions around 03:12 UTC. Error says permission denied: can_create_session.

audit-bot: alert: 2026-03-18T03:12:04Z role-matrix-v2 deploy -> 12,438 denied calls (threshold breached)

irene: Interesting timing — CloudKMS rotated a key at 03:11:50Z for the tokens service. Could be coincidence but worth checking if role claims decrypt failed.

leo: I pulled the migration diff from the deploy: looks like org-scoped grants were normalized. There's a line that strips the legacy "session.create" grant from the editor role at org-level:

```
-- migration: normalize_role_grants
UPDATE role_grants SET grants = array_remove(grants, 'session.create') WHERE scope = 'org' AND role = 'editor';
```

sam: oof. That matches the 403s. The script intended to collapse duplicate grants but missed the case where a composite grant depended on inheriting project-scope session.create.

maya: Any customers affected? We got two support tickets from sandbox orgs. No enterprise incidents yet.

nina: Prefer to canary rollback for affected tenants rather than full rollback. Can we hotfix the migration and re-apply the grant for orgs where sessions were used?

sam: I'm working on a PR to re-add the grant with a safe predicate: only when any project under org has session usage > 0. PR 3421. Added a smoke test to assert session creation for editor role.

irene: For forensics I'll correlate KMS events with the audit logs. If KMS rotate caused a JWT decrypt error, we'd see signature validation failures. I already found a handful of authfail logs at 03:12:01Z. Sample:

```
{"ts":"2026-03-18T03:12:01Z","service":"auth","msg":"jwt_decrypt_failed","uid":"u-1872","err":"invalid key version"}
```

leo: Two parallel issues then: 1) migration dropped a required grant, 2) auth cache/claims may have been serving tokens encrypted under old key. Fix plan: hotfix migration, backfill grants for affected orgs, invalidate auth caches on KMS rotate.

nina: Owners: sam -> hotfix & backfill, irene -> audit/KMS correlation, leo -> rollout gating & cache invalidation, maya -> customer comms.

sam: Deploying hotfix to canary now. Triggering deploy:

deploy-bot: deploy started for service:console-api, env:canary, sha: a1b2c3d (sam)

sam: Canary logs show session creation OK for tenant-243 and tenant-988 after grant reapply. No 403s in the last 5m.

maya: Drafted message to the two sandbox orgs explaining a temporary permission regression and mitigation steps. Holding until canary stable.

irene: Follow-up on KMS: I found that we didn't invalidate the auth cache when the KMS key version changed; tokens encrypted under the previous key remain trusted until TTL. Filing bug: AUTH-789 to add key-version check and cache invalidation hook on CloudKMS rotate.

leo: Also proposing a rollout change: don't run the normalize_role_grants migration without canary gating and a dry-run flag that prints affected orgs to logs for manual review. Add telemetry to count how many editors would lose grants before applying.

nina: Agreed. Add that as a hard precondition to future role-matrix migrations. Make the dry-run output part of the deploy log.

sam: Hotfix merged and promoted to prod rollback window. Rollout plan: 1) apply grant backfill, 2) enable canary for 10% orgs for 30m, 3) monitor 403 rate and latency, 4) full rollback if spike.

deploy-bot: canary deploy complete for canary group. monitor: https://deploys.internal/console-api/a1b2c3d

sam: Monitoring: 403 count dropped to baseline, session creation success up to 98%. Will start phased backfill in 10m.

irene: Audit exports created for the window 03:10-03:20 and pushed to secure bucket for postmortem. Link: https://s3.internal/reds/exports/2026-03-18/role-audit-0310-0320.json

maya: Notifying affected customers that fix is deployed and we'll follow up with a postmortem.

nina: After action items: 1) postmortem doc incl timeline & root cause, 2) add migration dry-run + telemetry, 3) AUTH-789 KMS cache invalidation, 4) add e2e test for session create via editor role, 5) retention check for audit logs. Assigning owners in pagerduty.

everyone: :thumbsup: :tada:
